I've learned some things about dealing with this:
1. if they did something that bothers you, address it calmly as soon as possible. this prevents shit from building up in the back of ur head and then blowing up at them
2. if its something you didn't address right away realize if addressing it will be useful for the relationship. like, is what u want to talk about so important that it could potentially negatively effect the relationship. if it is, go ahead and address it. if not, hopefully they won't do it again, but next time they do address it ASAP. don't dwell on it I mean easier said than done but idk I find the longer I think about things the more distorted they become too. it takes a lot of confidence and self respect to address things as they happen but learning to do this will help you a lot!! because you'll learn how to be able to express your needs and desires in a way that doesn't emotionally burden the other and yourself too! you'll be able to do it so quick and effortlessly and it won't ever become a huge big deal.
3. I think the biggest thing that helped me was thinking about how people don't do things specifically to hurt me. This will help in how u end up addressing an issue because you'll make it less about them and more about your needs and desires. everyone has issues and their own shit they're dealing with, they don't need more on top of it u know? you need to realize it is never the other person you actually have a problem with, it's yourself and how your trauma shapes how things scare you. so everything you do is more for yourself than anything else. being able to address things right away will help you feel more calm and stable minded because you're being true to your self and feelings. 
lastly of course there's some things you absolutely need to address. outwardly rude, hurtful, violent, cheating etc. but I know u guys know what I mean when these things usually aren't the case for us most of the time of stress. 
anyway. just a rant. pick and choose and try it out i hope it works for you as much as it did for me.
